description:
Find the AI-law rules (EU AI Act, US state AI laws, China, Korea and other markets) that apply to an AI feature
in a market, each with its cited provision and official link.

When to use: someone asks which laws, regulations or standards apply to what they are building, or where a kind of
AI feature is regulated (chatbot disclosure, hiring and employment decisions, credit or insurance decisions,
deepfakes and digital replicas, companion chatbots and minors, AI-generated content labels, training data).
The filters combine: a rule must cover one of the markets and one of the patterns given, and match the words if
any are given; each filter left out matches everything. Returns at most 10 rules,
most relevant first (the words matched, then the rules specific to the features, then binding law in force), each
with its lane, citation, official link, applies-from date and its page in the TwinEthos explorer. It does not sort
by date: use coming_into_force or recently_in_force for dates.
Limits: informational data, not legal advice.

features.description: The AI feature's integration patterns, any of: chat, rag, agentic, decision_pipeline (a model output that decides about a person), content_generation, classification, recommendation, embeddings. Omit it for every pattern.
features.title: Features

jurisdictions.description: Markets to cover, as codes: EU, a country code (GB, CN, KR, JP, BR, SG) or a US state as US-XX (US-CA, US-CO, US-NY); US matches every state. Omit it for every market.
jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions

limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 10 (default 10); `total` in the answer says how many matched.
limit.title: Limit

text.description: Words to match in rule titles, summaries and tags, such as disclosure, hiring or deepfake. Omit it to list every rule for the markets and patterns.
text.title: Text
